blocks.content:
A person is qualified if he or she:
• Is a citizen of India.
• Has been a High Court judge for at least 5 years, OR
• Has been an advocate in a High Court for at least 10 years, OR
• Is a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.
Is a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.

rows: Distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President

items: Note the duration difference: 5 years required for a High Court judge versus 10 years for a High Court advocate.
The 'distinguished jurist' provision depends strictly on the opinion of the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: An individual must be a citizen of India to be qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.
Requires a minimum of 5 years of experience as a High Court judge.
Alternatively, requires a minimum of 10 years of experience as an advocate in a High Court.
Can be appointed if recognized as a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.
